title: Budgeter rule retune + usage limit monitor (deferred Tier 2 work, bundled)
problem:
Two related budgeter weaknesses are currently sitting in loose TODOs (#10, #96) with no home ticket. Bundling them so the deferred work has a single tracked artifact.

(1) RULE PRECISION COLLAPSE. `budgeter/report.py --feedback` shows the warning system has 7% precision overall (3 true positives across 44 warnings, 41 false positives, 139 expensive tasks ran with NO warning). Several rules are net-negative — the unflagged baseline (20% precision) beats every combo containing scope_keywords. Specifically:
  - investigative_keywords (alone): 50% precision, 35,620 avg actual tokens. ONLY rule pulling its weight.
  - scope_keywords (alone): 0% precision, 3,465 avg. Drags every combo containing it below baseline.
  - step_count (alone): 17% precision, 9,034 avg. Net-negative.
  - file_count (alone): 36% precision, 28,764 avg. Marginal.

(2) NO USAGE-LIMIT VISIBILITY. We have no way to see how close we are to the Anthropic plan's usage cap. Budgeter tracks per-task token cost but cannot answer 'am I about to get rate-limited.' For Tier 4 unattended overnight runs, this is a real gap: a cron job that hits the cap at 3 AM has no graceful degradation path.

ADDITIONAL BLIND SPOT: Agent tool calls bypass pre_tool_use hooks, so subagent spawns (the actual expensive things in runners) are invisible to the warning system. Note: scribe note #188 has new data showing this is partially mitigated by post_tool_use logging, but the warning system still cannot WARN before a subagent spawn — only log its cost after the fact.
description:
Goal: budgeter warnings become genuinely useful (>50% precision) AND the user has visibility into Anthropic plan usage so Tier 4 cron jobs can degrade gracefully near the cap.

This ticket is deliberately bundled because the two pieces share a substrate (budgeter) and a goal (cost visibility for unattended runs). Splitting them duplicates context and risks one landing without the other.

Deliberately PUNTED until after Tier 5 (portability) lands. The user has explicitly decided that T3 -> T4 -> T5 takes precedence and that this T2 work needs more accumulated usage data before the rule retune is meaningful. Do not pull this ticket forward unless either (a) Tier 5 is complete or (b) the user explicitly reprioritizes.

Phase 1 — Rule retune (TODO #10)
- Drop or completely rewrite scope_keywords. Per the precision data, every combo containing it underperforms the unflagged baseline.
- Drop step_count alone. Keep only as a multiplier on investigative_keywords if a combo retune justifies it.
- Keep investigative_keywords as the only first-class signal — it's the only rule with >baseline precision on its own.
- Add new signals derived from the 139 missed-expensive-task analysis (Phase 2): likely candidates from prior thinking are large file reads, multi-file edits, deep grep searches, subagent spawns. Validate empirically against accumulated data, do not guess.
- Acceptance: budgeter warning precision rises to >50% on a held-out test set drawn from at least 100 expensive tasks.

Phase 2 — Missed-expensive-task analysis
- Re-run the analysis that produced the precision numbers above, but on a larger time window (1+ months of accumulated usage data, not the few days available today). The user explicitly said the deferral was 'we need more data first' — Phase 2 is the data-gathering this depends on.
- Output: a written analysis (scribe context note) identifying which task shapes the current rules miss, and what new signals would catch them. This is the input to Phase 1's new-signal design.
- Phase 2 MUST run before Phase 1's new-signal work, but Phases 1's negative-action items (drop scope_keywords + step_count) can land independently any time.

Phase 3 — Usage limit monitor (TODO #96)
- Anthropic does not expose a public API for plan usage percentage. Investigate approaches in this order:
  (a) Authenticated HTTP fetch of the console.anthropic.com usage page with cookies/session token. Cheapest if it works.
  (b) Browser automation via Playwright (already a stdlib-adjacent dependency, well-supported on Win/macOS/Linux). Heavier but reliable.
  (c) Manual paste workflow: a CLI that prompts the user to paste the usage page HTML/screenshot and parses it. Last resort.
- Whichever approach is chosen, the output is a Python module `budgeter/usage_monitor.py` that exposes `get_usage_pct() -> float | None`. None means 'unknown' — callers must handle it.
- Integration: budgeter pre_tool_use hook reads usage_pct on warning paths. If >80%, escalate the warning regardless of rule precision. If >95%, hard-block expensive operations (configurable threshold).
- For Tier 4 cron: the overnight runner checks usage_pct at start; if >70%, abort with a 'cap-near' summary instead of starting the run. Configurable.

Phase 4 — Bypass mitigation (subagent warning)
- Agent tool calls cannot fire pre_tool_use cost warnings today because they bypass the hook. Investigate whether the budgeter pre_tool_use hook can intercept Agent calls specifically by matcher='Agent' (similar to how harden's instrumentation works in scribe note #188's request_id plumbing).
- If yes: add a pre-spawn cost estimate based on the prompt size and target file size (per the cost-scaling formula in scribe note #188).
- If no: document the limitation and rely on post-spawn logging only.
- This phase is OPTIONAL for v1 — it can ship as a follow-up if Phases 1-3 are sufficient.
scope: budgeter/hooks/pre_tool_use.py (Phase 1 rule changes), budgeter/lib/* (Phase 2 analysis tooling), new budgeter/usage_monitor.py (Phase 3), runner/run.py or new cron entrypoint (Phase 3 integration for Tier 4), optional budgeter/hooks/pre_tool_use.py extension (Phase 4 Agent matcher). Test files alongside each module per repo convention.
